answer.label: In short
answer.lead: White-label ecommerce and Amazon services mean MMC manages your client's marketplace presence while you stay the agency of record. That covers listings, Amazon and quick commerce advertising, stock and content checks and reports. It suits D2C and consumer brands that sell on marketplaces as well as their own store.

stages.why: Weak titles and images waste ad spend, and the client points at the agency.
stages.does: We review the listing first and send you a short, ranked list of changes for the client to approve.

stages.breaks: Campaigns pile up with no clear job.
stages.why: A mix of manual and automatic campaigns hides what is earning.
stages.does: Campaigns are split by purpose and named so your team can read the account at a glance.

stages.breaks: Ads run while the stock runs out.
stages.why: Spend on a product that cannot ship hurts rank and the client's trust.
stages.does: We check availability against spend and warn you before a stockout, not after.

stages.breaks: The brand store is an afterthought.
stages.why: Shoppers who land on the brand's own page see a generic layout.
stages.does: We keep the store page and rich content in line with the client's brand sheet, with changes sent for approval.

stages.why: A good ad cost ratio does not mean the brand is growing.
stages.does: Reports show ad sales, total sales and margin together, so the story you tell is the whole one.
